text:
Beneath awnings of blond orange groves

the dusty road winds,

full of aromas and wind,

full of spring music.


At the first morning light

the cattle pass with their slow gait...

and the farmhand follows behind, dirty and begrimed,

riding his colt to the corrals.


Beside the old door he milks the udder,

and the fragrant, foaming milk

bubbles in the overflowing jar.

And the sun, in its local caress,

kindles the orange grove, fresh and sonorous,

as though it were throwing handfuls of gold...


Among the green foliage, the cabin

shows its rustic, thatched roof.

Beside it stands the golden-reed bamboo

creaking amid the tangled green.


In the distance the flexible cane rocks

its high plume, curled by the wind,

and as it undulates, its solid reed

raises the murmur of a strange song.


Amid so much beauty, nevertheless,

nothing inspires the soul with more sweetness

than that emerald distance,

embroidered with virgin thicket...

a hill rises there, and on its slope

a coconut palm waves its fan...

translation.title: Native Orchards
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the rural vocabulary, local vegetation, and the closing emerald distance and coconut palm; “la ubre ordeña” is rendered as the ordinary milking scene its syntax implies.
